references.text: Manasse was Joseph's firstborn son, and this verse confirms his position as the patriarch of the tribe of Manasseh.
Here Manasseh and Ephraim are mentioned as Joseph's sons born in Egypt, which establishes Manasseh's lineage.
Machir, the son of Manasseh, is mentioned here, and his children were born on Joseph's knees, confirming the lineage.
Machir is mentioned as the son of Manasseh, and the clan of the Machirites descends from him.
The lineage from Manasseh through Machir and Gilead is confirmed in connection with the daughters of Zelophehad.
Machir's sons conquered Gilead, and Moses gave them the land, explaining why Gilead belonged to them.
Moses gave Gilead and Bashan to half of the tribe of Manasseh, specifically to the descendants of Machir.
Describes the inheritance portion of half of the descendants of Manasseh, including Gilead and Bashan, given to Machir's sons.
Machir, the son of Manasseh, is mentioned as the father of Gilead, and his connection to the region of Gilead is confirmed.
The genealogy of Machir and his role as the firstborn of Manasseh are further detailed, along with Gilead's connection.
